test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is regarded as an accounting convention and NOT as an accounting concept?
solution:
The correct answer is** Conservatism.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Conservatism:**

 
 
• The conservatism principle, also known as prudence, is an accounting convention that advises accountants to exercise caution and choose solutions that result in lower profits and asset valuations. This principle aims to prevent the overstatement of financial health.
 
• It ensures that uncertainties and risks are adequately reflected in financial statements, promoting reliability and accuracy.
 
• For example, if there are two equally probable outcomes for a future event, the one that is less likely to overstate assets and income should be chosen.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Going concern:**

 
 
• This accounting concept assumes that a business will continue to operate indefinitely, or at least for the foreseeable future. It implies that the company has no intention or need to liquidate or significantly curtail its operations.
 
 
 
• **Money measurement:**
 
 
• This concept states that only those transactions and events that can be measured in monetary terms are recorded in the financial statements. Non-monetary items like employee skills or customer satisfaction are not recorded.
 
 
 
• **Accounting period:**
 
 
• This concept divides the life of an enterprise into time periods, such as months, quarters, or years, for the purpose of preparing financial statements. It ensures that financial performance and position are reported periodically.
